evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 12.03 mg/L, far above minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0, no declining trend toward a constraint
Receiving P assay at t=48 h (available 52.0 h) = 2.843 g/L, consistent with source batches source-1 (3.057), source-2 (3.017), source-3 (2.979) at same age
Receiving trajectory matches all three source batches' lag/growth patterns (e.g., dip near 24 h, recovery at 28 h), indicating a healthy, in-family run
No measurement anomalies or stalls in receiving DO2/P history up to the 52 h decision time
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows no anomaly: DO2 is ~12 mg/L at t=52 h (vs 2.0 mg/L minimum), and the delayed product assay P(48h)=2.84 g/L matches the source batches (~2.98–3.06 g/L) at the same process age. Growth is on the normal trajectory. Reducing feed or stopping would sacrifice product mass; increasing air is unnecessary since no oxygen constraint is approached. Any bounded intervention here adds risk without expected benefit, so the least-risk, mass-retaining action is to keep conditions unchanged.
submission.uncertainty: The forward physical model was not queried and hidden receiving parameters may differ from the source process; a modest lag or difference in late-run oxygen demand cannot be excluded. However, current DO2 margin is ~10 mg/L above the constraint, so the risk of a KEEP decision leading to an oxygen violation before the next control point is very low.
